title: Construction of 2-D Z-Complementary Array Code Sets with Flexible Lengths for Different System Requirements: the 2-D ZCACS construction (Theorem 1)
author: Abhishek Roy
work: Construction of 2-D Z-Complementary Array Code Sets with Flexible Lengths for Different System Requirements
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the paper’s headline construction: it asserts that the family of arrays built from the IGC code set is a 2-D ZCAC of size L_1 x L_2 with ZCZ size Z_1 x Z_2 and flock size M, and that the whole family is a 2-D ZCACS of set size K, with all parameters computed from the prime factorisation of the lengths. Its 185-line proof is the author’s own and is not a citation. With the IGC construction lemma (the retained context Lemma 5) and the imported complementary-mate lemma supplied as prerequisites, the author must still carry out the whole correlation analysis: expand each array entry as a q-th root of unity raised to the exponent built from the EBF functions, split the inner sum over j into the three ranges S_1, S_2, S_3 at the boundaries prod p_alpha^{m_alpha} - tau_2 and prod p_alpha^{m_alpha}, prove separately that each of the three sums vanishes for tau_2 not equal to 0 by reducing them to the zero-correlation identity of the IGC lemma, treat the exceptional case tau_2 = 0 by a second splitting into T_1 and T_2 and an explicit evaluation of the two resulting sums as prod p_alpha^{m_alpha}, handle the W_1/W_2 parity terms coming from the last Z_2-coordinate, and finally close the tau_1 not equal to 0 and tau_1 = 0 cases by the complementary-mate property of the GCP pairs. That prolonged, case-by-case exponential-sum verification of a new construction is engineering-mathematics research rather than a qualification exercise, while the individual steps are elementary root-of-unity manipulations, which places the unit in the middle of the scale.
